newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO SCORES ON RETURN AS ITALY BEAT POLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO SCORES ON RETURN AS ITALY BEAT POLAND.

text.p: Roberto Baggio, displaying more than a touch of genius, scored on his return to international soccer on Wednesday as Italy swept aside Poland 3-0 in a World Cup European group two qualifier.

The ponytailed AC Milan midfielder, dropped by former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi in late 1995, dodged and sidestepped defenders to fire in a breathtaking solo goal just 12 minutes after his arrival as a substitute.

Baggio's 63rd minute goal was the third and last of the evening and kept Italy top of the group and unbeaten on 16 points without having conceded a goal since the veteran Cesare Maldini took over from Sacchi at the start of the year.
Chelsea midfielder Roberto Di Matteo had opened the scoring with his first international goal in the 23rd minute with a half-volleyed shot off a Demetrio Albertini cross.
Captain Paolo Maldini, playing his 80th match for Italy, made it 2-0 in the 37th minute with a scooped shot into the back of the net after a flicked-on header from Ciro Ferrara.
Poland goalkeeper Andrzej Wozniak blocked Maldini's first shot but the son of coach Cesare was ready for the rebound at the post.
